title: From need to action: plan, fund and share a community project

say: From need to action: plan, fund and share a community project.
This is the video for Module 3 of Leadership, Identity, and Community Development.
Community development means people working together to improve conditions in their own community.

panel.heading: Community development, asset first
items: Small, visible and trusted beats large

say: Asset-Based Community Development starts by mapping what the community already has, not only what it lacks. People described only by their needs tend to wait for rescue. People who see their assets start acting.

panel.heading: Community development, asset first
items: Small, visible and trusted beats large

say: So use your own knowledge and resources first, and outside help second.

panel.heading: Community development, asset first
items: Small, visible and trusted beats large

say: Your project does not need to be large. A small project people can see and trust is the best foundation for bigger ones.

panel.heading: Community development, asset first
items: Small, visible and trusted beats large

say: First, listen and look. Walk the area, ask at least 10 people what would make life better and what they are willing to do. Then map your assets. Individuals, like a retired teacher or youths with phones and data.

say: Associations, like the women's fellowship, the town union and cooperatives.

say: For example, Chioma's street in Port Harcourt has 30 households and floods every rainy season. Flooding is the trunk of her problem tree.

panel.heading: Problem tree to SMART goal
items: Choose one root cause you can act on

say: Ask why, several times. The roots: refuse dumped in the gutter, and no regular clearing.

panel.heading: Problem tree to SMART goal
items: Choose one root cause you can act on

say: The branches are the effects: lost sales, damaged goods, and stagnant water that breeds mosquitoes.

panel.heading: Problem tree to SMART goal
items: Choose one root cause you can act on

say: Choose a root cause your group can act on. Treating only an effect means facing the same trouble next season.

panel.heading: Problem tree to SMART goal
items: Choose one root cause you can act on
panel.rule: Fix a root cause, or you will be back next season.

say: Then write a goal that is Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant and Time-bound. Chioma's: by the end of June, residents will clear the main gutter on the first Saturday of every month.
Test it: could a neighbour tell, on a fixed date, whether it was achieved?

panel.heading: Problem tree to SMART goal
items: Choose one root cause you can act on
panel.rule: Fix a root cause, or you will be back next season.

say: Now cost it fully. 12 residents will work, a church compound will store the tools, and a neighbour with a pickup will carry waste to the approved dumpsite.

say: On clearing day, safety comes first. Wear gloves and closed shoes or boots. Never handle broken glass or sharp metal with bare hands. Keep children away, and do not enter fast-flowing water.
Wash with soap and clean water afterwards, and never dump waste into a river or canal.

panel.heading: Working safely on clean-ups
items: Gloves and closed shoes or boots
No bare hands on glass or sharp metal
Keep children away from the work
Waste to an approved dumpsite only

say: Know your stakeholders: anyone who can help or block you. Visit the community head first, as local protocol expects. Work closely with high-power, high-interest people like the CDA chairman. Then write to officials in five parts. Start with who you are.

panel.heading: A request letter in five parts

say: Show what you have already done. 30 households contributed 51,000 naira and cleared the gutter.

panel.heading: A request letter in five parts

say: Make one specific ask, such as weekly refuse collection from a named point.

panel.heading: A request letter in five parts
panel.rule: Show your own effort first, then make one clear ask.

say: Say why it matters, then give a name, a phone number and the date you will follow up. And post your accounts after every activity. Officials support groups that keep honest records.

panel.heading: A request letter in five parts
panel.rule: Show your own effort first, then make one clear ask.

say: Your capstone starts with a reflection in three questions. What happened? Halima spoke up 9 times in four weeks.

cards.d: What happened. Halima spoke up 9 times in four weeks and her monthly dues idea was adopted.
What it means, linked to your values. Preparing her point in writing made her calm and clear.
What you will do next. Hold her point once more when challenged, and ask for a vote.

say: So what? What did it mean, and what did you learn? Be honest about what did not go well.

say: Now what? What will you do differently? Back it with evidence: minutes, receipts, attendance lists and photos taken with consent.

say: To remember. Map assets first. Act on a root cause. Cost the project fully and report balances every time. Show your effort before you ask.
And name a deputy from month 1, so the project does not depend only on you.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Act on a root cause you can reach
Cost it fully and report every naira
Show your effort, then make one ask

say: Now do a community walk, draw a problem tree and write a SMART goal with a budget. Map your stakeholders and write one request. Then assemble your reflection, evidence and 90-day plan.
